manifest.name: Text
manifest.purpose: Renders text in a named typographic role and tone. Every string on screen goes through it; nothing else sets font size or colour.
manifest.description: The typography primitive. `variant` picks size, line height, weight and tracking from the type scale; `tone` picks the colour; `as` picks the HTML element for semantics. `numeric` switches on tabular numerals and the 7:1 numeric colour for money, counts and dates.

as.description: Rendered element. Choose for meaning: h2 for a section title, label for a field, time for a date.
as.a11y: Heading levels must not skip (h2 then h3). A label must point at a control with htmlFor.

variant.description: Typographic variant from the scale. Independent of the element, so an h2 can use heading-sm in a dense panel.

tone.description: Colour. primary and numeric meet 7:1; the rest meet 4.5:1 on every surface in both themes.

align.description: Text alignment. Money columns align end.

numeric.description: Tabular numerals plus the numeric colour (unless tone is set). Use for every number that will be compared or summed.

truncate.a11y: Truncated text must be available in full elsewhere (a title attribute or a tooltip).

a11y.role: none (inherits the element's role: heading, paragraph, label, time). The HTML role attribute passes through.
a11y.name: Not applicable; Text is content. For label, the name is the text and it names the control via htmlFor.
notes: Pick `as` for document structure first; use `role` for size. Screen readers navigate by heading level, not by font size.
Do not convey status by tone alone; pair a tone with words or an icon with a label.

rules: All text goes through Text. Never apply text-* or font-* utilities to raw elements.
Money, counts and dates use numeric (or a numeric-* role) so columns line up.
label elements use htmlFor and point at the control's id.
dos: Use heading-sm for card titles and panel headers.
Use caption with tone="muted" for helper text under a field.
donts: Do not use display roles inside cards or tables.
Do not use tone="muted" for anything the user must read to act (errors, amounts).

examples.name: Money
examples.description: Tabular numerals, end aligned, numeric colour.
